STYLE: Black-and-white coloring-book line art: clean black outlines on a pure white background. No shading, no gray, and no solid black fills — leave every region open and unfilled so it can be colored in.
PRINTED_PAGE: This drawing is printed on a larger sheet with white paper all around it. Fill the canvas edge to edge with the scene, but resolve the composition inside it: keep the linework a little clear of all four edges, and let every form close rather than running off the edge or being cut by it.
UNLETTERED_PAGE: Do not letter the page: no title, no caption, no plate or figure number, no key or legend, no species name, no motto, no signature, no lettered panel or cartouche — anywhere on the page, inside a border or outside it. A border or frame is a border and nothing else. Any words this drawing carries come from the scene described below; the page has none of its own.
CHARACTER_SHEET_ANCHOR: Image 1 is the character reference sheet — it fixes exactly how each character looks: the same face, markings, colours, proportions, outfit, and props. Match it for whatever part of a character the scene shows, and do NOT redesign, restyle, age, or re-color anyone. This fixes how a character is drawn, not how much of one is in frame: when the scene crops a character — a face filling a close-up, only the paws and hands in an insert shot — draw just that part at the size the scene asks, and never widen the shot or add the rest of the character or their face to keep it in view.
PRIOR_PAGE_ANCHOR: Image 2 is an earlier page of the same book, included ONLY so the characters keep looking like themselves. Do NOT reuse its composition, camera angle, poses, background, props or supporting cast. This is a different moment in the story and must read as a different picture.
SUBORDINATE_DETAIL: If the scene places a plant, branch, vine, or other decorative detail beside or around the main subject, keep it a small accent, not a feature: draw it once and simply, tucked into a corner or a narrow strip along one edge, taking up well under a quarter of the page. It stays clearly smaller than what the page is about, and must never spread across the frame, climb a whole side of the page top to bottom, or fan out into a dense spray that rivals the main subject.
SHEET_NO_TEXT: Draw only the characters: no words, letters, labels, captions, names, headers, titles, callouts, watermarks or signatures anywhere on the sheet.
FREE_PAGE_PORTRAYAL: Keep the subject simple, friendly, and age-appropriate: bold, chunky shapes a young child can color, nothing dense or intricate.
